principles: Keep the first implementation slice mechanically useful but non-blocking by default.
Register every new command and artifact in the real CLI/process-fact surfaces instead of relying on docs or prompt text.
Preserve progressive hardening: start from Intent MVP and add diagnostics only when triggers require them.
drivers: User approved development but explicitly asked not to keep adding concepts.
M0-M2 must not accidentally implement or enforce M5-M9 behavior.
Existing Lattice gates require command policy, lifecycle phase allowlists, handler registration, and process-fact contract alignment.
Tests must prove dry-run diagnostics report would-block gaps without changing lifecycle state.

options.name: A: dedicated ProofStory MVP handler and core helper
pros: Keeps new artifact schemas and diagnostics isolated from unrelated handlers.
Makes orphan-surface and process-fact registration straightforward.
Allows later M3-M9 work to extend the same bounded module.
cons: Adds a small new handler/core module pair instead of extending an existing planning handler.

options.name: B: fold all MVP commands into understanding or story handlers
pros: Fewer files in the short term.
Can reuse existing store and story validation patterns directly.
cons: Mixes intent artifact semantics into unrelated handlers and makes future ProofStory growth harder to audit.

chosen: A: dedicated ProofStory MVP handler and core helper
rationale: Choose a dedicated ProofStory MVP handler/core helper because the new commands form a coherent process-fact surface. This keeps M0-M2 isolated, makes registration and tests explicit, and avoids silently turning understanding_set into a generic ProofStory container.

preMortem.scenario: Dry-run diagnostics accidentally become an enforce gate for ordinary stories.
preMortem.trigger: proofstory_gate_check is wired into story_advance or lifecycle guards during the MVP story.
preMortem.consequence: Small tasks get blocked by incomplete ProofStory artifacts, violating the observe/warn rollout principle.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep proofstory_gate_check read-only/dry-run only in this story; do not call it from machine.ts or story_advance gates.

preMortem.scenario: Milestone ledger triggers from isolated keywords and creates false positives.
preMortem.trigger: Classification treats any word like complete or DONE as multi-deliverable intent without structure or semantic signal.
preMortem.consequence: A small request such as a typo fix receives unnecessary milestone diagnostics.
preMortem.mitigation: Implement classification with structural/semantic triggers: explicit counts, numbered lists, all milestones/items, subsystem removal, end-to-end behavior, or provided ledger items.

preMortem.scenario: Process-fact registration drifts from handler/schema registration.
preMortem.trigger: New commands are added to handlers and CLI schemas but omitted from command policy, phase allowlist, catalog, or process-fact levels.
preMortem.consequence: CLI help, lifecycle permission, and contract verification disagree, causing hard-to-debug gate failures.
preMortem.mitigation: Update command policy, config phase tools, command catalog/schema, registry, process-fact levels/registry, and add a focused smoke test plus process-fact/orphan-surface verification.
